correctness.rationale: The viewing-ray inverse is θ ↦ θ−arcsin(r sin θ), so its angular density, uniform first-order tilt, and semicircle masses follow by differentiation. A non-containing triangle has exactly one anchor with the other two rays in its forward semicircle. Integrating the squared semicircle mass, the terms involving derivatives of powers of arcsin integrate to zero, yielding the exact radial mean. The origin pair projection is minor separation (in turns) minus 1/4; exact integration gives the stated spectrum and squared kernel norm 1/48. The count has pair coefficient n−2; the uniform canonical triple remainder divided by n² vanishes in L², and the bounded likelihood second moment transfers this and the spectral truncation error in probability. The bounded Fourier-coordinate CLT shifts only the first cosine by −c/√2; the diagonal correction is one per coordinate. This gives the displayed chaos and both its moments. For √n r_n→∞, the first projection divided by r_n tends uniformly to 2 cos θ/π²; its variance tends to 2/π⁴. The coefficient binom(n−1,2) gives outer variance 1/(2π⁴), and the canonical higher terms are negligible since n r_n²→∞. At √n r_n→0 the likelihood converges to one in L². The claims use the stated distinct centerings and are pointwise/deterministic-sequence limits, not a uniform process limit.
residual_risks: The supplied numerical checker is supplementary; for example, its finite variance and limit moment sections evaluate formulas rather than independently prove them. Weak convergence rests on the analytic argument.

value.rationale: Depth-based location inference needs calibration precisely where the center's degenerate law ceases to approximate the statistic, yet an off-center fixed-radius CLT is not uniform. The scale, one-mode noncentrality, exact population centering and outer variance give quantitative answers to that gap even in this narrow benchmark.
